episodes.183271: Two clusters of storms pushed northeastward across the Lower Susquehanna Valley during the evening of September 8, 2023, each producing sporadic wind damage across York and Lancaster Counties.
episodes.183272: A mesoscale convective vortex (MCV) pushed across northwestern Pennsylvania and into New York state during the morning and afternoon hours of September 9, 2023. A broken line of showers and storms developed by late morning over the western highlands, and progressed eastward through the afternoon hours. Additional storms developed ahead of this broken line. This activity resulted in locally heavy rain and isolated wind damage.
episodes.183282: An upper trough situated from the Great Lakes through the Tennessee Valley provided the instability to support very slow-moving showers and thunderstorms that drifted across the central Appalachians into the lower Mid-Atlantic.  During the afternoon of the 9th, a surface trough had developed from Surry County, NC northward through Montgomery County, VA into southeast West Virginia, providing the low level convergence needed to support prolonged thunderstorm activity. A southerly wind flow carried deep moisture northward from the Carolina coast during the afternoon, with precipitable water values observed in the 1.5 to 1.6 inch range across Montgomery County, while surface-based CAPE values were observed in the 1,000 to 1,200 J/Kg range.  Steering winds were less than 10 knots from the south, leading to slow storm movement.  Several personal weather stations indicated that the vast majority of rainfall occurred during a 2-hour period beginning around 1 PM EDT, with rainfall falling at rates of 4 to 6 inches per hour. CREST Unit Streamflow in the town of Blacksburg near the headwaters of Cedar Run peaked at 19Z at around 1,000 cfs/sec/mi^2, while the three-hour Average Recurrence Interval was nearing a 200-year event.

episodes.183517: Southerly flow brought elevated dewpoints in the 70s to southern New England leading to a heat advisory. All the heat and humidity led to good instability which, along with forcing from a strong mid level jet produced severe storms in Massachusetts and Connecticut and some flash flooding in Massachusetts.
episodes.183519: In the midst of very warm and humid weather a hand full of thunderstorms caused some wind damage and flooding. The environment had very weak forcing so even though there was a good amount of CAPE there were only a few storms that became severe.

episodes.183911: Upper level system brings slow moving thunderstorms to southwest Virginia, with one thunderstorm producing damaging winds.
episodes.183936: Thunderstorms brought locally heavy rain to Camden County on the afternoon of September 9.  Rainfall totals were as high as 2.5 to 3.5 inches.
episodes.184154: A weak disturbance supported scattered thunderstorms across Northeastern Pennsylvania. While instability was weak, there was enough to supported a couple of severe thunderstorms. Damaging wind gusts knocked down trees and wires throughout the region.
episodes.184242: A late summer pattern prevailed with scattered thunderstorms producing occasional gusty winds across the coastal waters with waterspouts also reported.
episodes.184447: Unsettled weather was on the docket each afternoon from September 9th through the 12th across West Virginia as a result of a stationary frontal boundary residing over the area. While severe parameters were not impressive during this time frame, afternoon thunderstorms had enough gumption to promote isolated tree and power line damage across parts of the state. High moisture levels festering over these several days also resulted in high water issues along local roads, especially in Raleigh County, where flood prone areas in the Beckley area took on a decent amount of street flooding on September 10th. Convection was primarily diurnally driven during this time, so the severe and flash flooding concerns quickly tapered down after sunset each day.
episodes.184450: In the midst of a passing upper level disturbance and nearby surface boundary, the afternoon of September 9th observed strong to severe thunderstorms in southwest Virginia. Isolated instances of damaging wind gusts took place in the region, with a storm in Dickenson County growing strong enough to result in downed trees within the county. High moisture levels were also in place that afternoon, so heavy downpours were not out of the question. This, coupled with the slow nature of storms, led to high water concerns outside the town of Prater in Buchanan County due to drain pipes becoming washed out.
episodes.184464: On September 6th, a cold front entered into West Virginia and stirred up showers and thunderstorms for the afternoon. One storm in particular that passed through Fayette County was strong enough to cause two trees and power lines to be blown down. The severe threat quickly diminished as drier air filtered in behind the frontal passage.||Another weak cold front arrived two days later on the 8th, this time imposing a flash flooding threat. Despite the front having already crossed much of West Virginia by the afternoon, there was still enough lift along the foothills and mountains that promoted slow moving showers and storms. Enough rain fell in McDowell County that resulted in high water along a local road for a few hours.
episodes.184759: An influx of moisture restarted a brief active period moving towards the middle of September. As a result, the region saw a couple of days with scattered showers and thunderstorms, some of which produced strong gusty winds, with one producing a landspout.
episodes.184779: An increase in monsoon moisture brought strong thunderstorms over northern Arizona.  One thunderstorm produced a landspout tornado.
episodes.184927: An upper trough situated from the Great Lakes through the Tennessee Valley provided the instability to support very slow-moving showers and thunderstorms that drifted across the central Appalachians into the lower Mid-Atlantic. During the afternoon of the 9th, a surface trough had developed from Surry County, NC northward through Montgomery County, VA into southeast West Virginia, providing the low level convergence needed to support prolonged thunderstorm activity. Southerly wind flow carried deep moisture northward from the Carolina coast during the afternoon, with precipitable water values near 1.5 inches across Surry County, while surface-based CAPE values were observed in the 1,000 to 1,200 J/Kg range. Steering winds were less than 10 knots from the south, leading to slow storm movement.
episodes.185565: Isolated severe thunderstorms developed across portions of the Concho Valley and Heartland producing damaging winds. Also, a significant microburst occurred in Taylor County on September 5th.
episodes.185586: A good bit of moisture worked its way into the combined Oklahoma and Texas Panhandles on the 9th through the 11th. The upper level pattern favored upper level help for storms to travel into the combined Panhandles from the west and northwest during the late afternoon into overnight hours. The first night on the 9th a couple of strong supercell thunderstorms dropped hail up to 2.5 in diameter in the western Oklahoma Panhandle. More widespread storms managed to drop hail up to 1.5, but these storms also produced several severe wind gusts upwards of 80 plus mph on the night of the 10th across much of the combined Panhandles.
episodes.185643: An upper-level trough over the Tennessee valley and a stalled frontal boundary over western North Carolina and Virginia combined with a surface trough over the Coastal Plain of central North Carolina brought several rounds of showers and thunderstorms. Flash flooding and damaging winds were reported in Wake, Halifax, and Forsyth counties.
episodes.185647: Scattered thunderstorms developed along a stationary front which was located over the central Sandhills, around 1 PM CDT on September 9th. This activity quickly became severe and tracked to the southeast into Custer County. Additional thunderstorm activity developed over Logan County and northern Lincoln County and tracked south into eastern Hayes and Frontier Counties through the early evening hours. Several hail reports, up to two inches in diameter and wind gusts up to 70 MPH occurred.
episodes.185686: Scattered severe thunderstorms in advance of a frontal boundary produced damaging winds across portions of central and south central Virginia.
episodes.185704: Scattered severe thunderstorms in advance of a frontal boundary produced damaging winds across portions of central and southeast Virginia.
episodes.185705: Scattered severe thunderstorms in advance of a frontal boundary produced damaging winds across portions of northeast North Carolina.
episodes.185751: Scattered thunderstorms in advance of a frontal boundary produced gusty winds across portions of the Chesapeake Bay.
episodes.185752: Scattered thunderstorms in advance of a frontal boundary produced gusty winds across portions of the York River.
episodes.185753: Scattered thunderstorms in advance of a frontal boundary produced gusty winds across portions of the James River.
episodes.185759: A frontal boundary and low pressure system located to the west and east of eastern New York was the focus for rounds of showers and thunderstorms each day September 7-9. Strong to severe thunderstorms were more widespread on September 7-8. These storms resulted in numerous reports of tree and powerline damage, as well as thousands without power and several road closures. Some school districts across Columbia County delayed classes or closed on September 8 as a result of the severe thunderstorms on September 7.
episodes.185774: During the afternoon hours, an isolated thunderstorm developed over Cheyenne County, Kansas and moved southeast across the area. More scattered storms developed over portions of extreme Southwest Nebraska and East-Central Colorado, moving south-southeast through the evening hours. These storms produced large hail up to the size of limes and thunderstorm wind gusts of 58 to 77 mph. The largest hail was reported in Wheeler while the strongest wind gusts were observed in Gove County where three semi trucks were also rolled over.
episodes.185816: With continued southwesterly flow aloft, another disturbance moved through, into a hot, humid, and unstable airmass. This resulted in the development of strong to severe thunderstorms in parts of eastern Pennsylvania, which produced damaging wind gusts and large hail.
episodes.185817: With continued southwesterly flow aloft, another disturbance moved through, into a hot, humid, and unstable airmass. This resulted in the development of strong to severe thunderstorms in parts of Delaware, which produced large hail.
episodes.185818: A stalled frontal boundary over New Jersey resulted in the development of a few strong to severe thunderstorms in parts of the state. Storms produced large hail and damaging wind gusts.
episodes.185819: A stalled frontal boundary over Delaware resulted in the development of a few strong to severe thunderstorms in parts of the state. Storms produced damaging wind gusts.
episodes.185820: A stalled frontal boundary over Maryland resulted in the development of a few strong to severe thunderstorms in parts of the state. Storms produced damaging wind gusts.
episodes.185871: A stationary front positioned roughly from New York to the Gulf Coast led to several rounds of showers and thunderstorms in the Piedmont of Virginia. An upper level storm system combined with daytime heating helped increased the coverage of storms during the afternoon and evening hours, while low level convergence along the front focused the thunderstorm activity near the mountains.
episodes.185874: A stationary front remained over the Mid Atlantic region and led to multiple rounds of thunderstorms. While wind shear was weak, instability was high creating a favorable environment for localized damaging winds during the late morning and afternoon hours.
episodes.185875: A stationary front remained over the Mid Atlantic region and led to multiple rounds of thunderstorms. While wind shear was weak, instability was high creating a favorable environment for localized damaging winds during the late morning and afternoon hours.
episodes.185877: A stationary frontal system over northeastern Pennsylvania combined with a weak upper level disturbance to focus heavy rain producing thunderstorms over the area. Torrential downpours over just a couple of hours accumulated between 3 to 5 inches of rainfall in small stream basins above the large metropolitan area known as the Lackawanna-Wyoming Valley. Severe flash flooding resulted in many road and bridge washouts around the local region. Motorists were stranded on urban streets and the flooding resulted in the deaths of two people who attempted to evacuate their vehicle into rushing waters. Another four people were seriously injured when their vehicle crashed into the remnants of a washed out bridge. The perpetual thunderstorms and flooding also shut down the Luzerne County Fair. Overall damages to the region as a result of this severe flooding are estimated at around 20 million dollars.
episodes.185902: North and Central Texas were situated beneath the eastern flank of a mid and upper level high pressure ridge during the early to middle part of the month. Multiple disturbances within the flow aloft, along with a weak surface front, resulted in thunderstorm development each day during the weekend of Sept 8-11. A few of these storms became severe with mainly damaging downburst winds.
episodes.185940: A weakening upper-level trough over the Florida Peninsula created an early start for convection as showers and storms began to develop in the morning hours over the Atlantic Ocean.
episodes.185941: A weakening upper-level trough over the Florida Peninsula created an atmosphere that was conducive for diurnal convection as showers and storms developed along sea-breeze boundaries.
episodes.185976: A gradual increase in northwesterly flow occurred across the Southern Plains during the day on September 8th. At the same time, a weak surface low and cold front shifted south with a notable wind shift extending into far Northeast Texas. Very hot surface temperatures were observed to the south of the boundary with maximum values in excess of 105 degrees. As a result, the boundary layer was very deep across this area with strong and increasingly stretched thunderstorm updrafts resulting from the peak of late afternoon/early evening heating and instability. Eventually, a report of large hail up to ping pong ball size was received in association with a severe thunderstorm in Red River County.
episodes.185986: A broad upper-level disturbance initiated scattered shower and thunderstorms across North and North-Central GA during the early afternoon hours. Minor instability meant a few thunderstorms became strong to severe. Storms were slow moving and reached the eastern portion of the CWA late in the evening. Late storm consolidation led to isolated severe wind and flooding.
episodes.186112: An isolated waterspout was observed south of the Saddlebunch Keys in association with a convective cloud line near the Lower Florida Keys.
episodes.186172: A cluster of thunderstorms developed around downtown Charleston and the Charleston Harbor around sunrise ahead of a stationary front. The thunderstorms produced strong wind gusts in Charleston Harbor.
episodes.186190: A lingering frontal boundary initiates convection over northeast New Jersey, with an upper level trough axis remaining just to the west. Some storms became severe and produced damaging winds over northeast NJ.
